To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

feedback is a special type of speech act, which is context sensitive in the sense that it depends on the type of speech acts, the factual polarity and information status of the utterance to which it is a reaction.

feedback utterances are speech acts which are context sensitive in the sense that their interpretation depends on the interpretation of the preceding utterances, that the context sensitivity of the interpretation of feedback expressions is due to their pragmatic content (i. e. the type of speech acts they convey, the information they give about the communicative status, and their factual polarity), and that the context sensitivity can be formalized in a situation semantics framework.

(1) feedback utterances convey information about the communicative functions of the preceding utterances, (2) the information conveyed by feedback utterance is of different levels of awareness and intention, (3) the interpretation of feedback expressions is context sensitive in that the type of speech acts, the factual polarity, and the information status influence the interpretation of the feedback expressions.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the interpretation of feedback expressions depends on the interpretation of the preceding utterances, and that this interpretation is context-sensitive, i.e., it depends on the context in which these utterances occur, and on the way the participants use the feedback expressions.
